pNone_chapter_1: In a dimly lit library filled with towering wooden bookshelves and scattered stacks of parchment, Byomkesh Bakshi sits hunched over a large mahogany desk. He wears a crisp white dhoti-kurta and holds a smoldering cigarette, his sharp eyes fixed intently on a magnifying glass held over a document. Beside him stands the sturdier Ajit, dressed in similar traditional attire, resting a firm hand on Byomkesh's shoulder as if to pull him away from his work. Warm orange light from a desk lamp casts long shadows across the floor, contrasting with the fading blue twilight visible through a large open window. The air is thick with the quiet stillness of deep intellectual concentration and the soft haze of tobacco smoke.
